content.text: Notable: `Math.max(0, findIndex(...))` when no active course exists returns 0, silently misdirecting hours to course 0 instead of failing. Let me note that and continue.

`buildTrainingPlanAllocationIncreaseLineItems` at line 405-412 pairs `previousItems[index]` with `nextItems[index]` by array position, not by any stable key. If array ordering ever differs between the two snapshots (e.g. new lines appended in different order, or a line removed), this silently mispairs and either misses added hours or invents phantom ones. Worth flagging as MEDIUM/HIGH depending on caller guarantees. Let me check callers later. Continuing.

At line 145-147, `itemAmountCents > definitionTotalCents` catches an excess but there's no handling if `definitionTotalCents > itemAmountCents` (definitions summing to more than the parent fee item) — that excess is silently absorbed with no adjustment, meaning `unallocatedFeeCents` under-counts and per-certificate totals could overstate the actual fee. Let me note and continue.

`getLocalDateOnly` uses `date.getFullYear()`/`getMonth()`/`getDate()` — these are local-timezone getters — while dates are stored as UTC date-only strings parsed as `T00:00:00.000Z`. This creates a timezone mismatch: "today" is computed in the server's local timezone but compared against UTC-anchored dates. If deployed on a US server (behind UTC) this shifts the "today" boundary by hours, potentially misclassifying a course as 'upcoming'/'past_target' a day early/late near midnight. Worth flagging as MEDIUM.
`buildCertificateLenderMilestones` line 111 `Math.floor(totalCents / certificates.length)` then last certificate absorbs remainder — fine, standard remainder distribution. Looks solid. Continuing.
This one looks well-designed with a clear protective invariant. Continuing.

Line 108: same local-vs-UTC "today" mismatch as `training-plan-course-schedule.ts` — `getStatus` uses local `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` compared against a `dueDate` string that's presumably a date-only (UTC-anchored) value elsewhere in the app. Same class of bug, second occurrence — worth flagging as a pattern (duplicated logic, no shared helper).

`getCertificateHours` line 149: `Math.max(instructionHours, equipmentHours)` — this silently discards whichever is smaller rather than validating they should match, per the adjustments file's own comment ("Instruction and equipment lines intentionally receive the same hour total"). If they legitimately diverge due to a bug elsewhere, this masks it rather than surfacing a discrepancy. Low-medium confidence, worth noting as a data-integrity blind spot.

This confirms the same "no active course found → falls back to index 0" pattern is repeated here too (line 336-338, though this one at least tries `hours_complete` before `[0]`, more defensible than allocation.ts's `Math.max(0, findIndex())`). Also `total <= 0` at line 377 means a guardrail with total=0 hours is silently skipped — but that matches allocation.ts's convention that 0 total = "complete"/no limit, so intentional.

Now checking `parseTrainingAllocationHoldMetadata` — the fallback JSON.parse of `notes.split('\n')[0]` is a defensive parse for legacy data, reasonable.
Clean, well-documented file, limitations noted honestly. No findings here. Now the largest file — quote PDF.
